title: Q1: Employee Salary Processing
body:
**Difficulty: Medium. Phase: 2.**

### Problem

A payroll system has different employee types, and salary depends on the type.

### Required design

- abstract class Employee with private int employeeId and String employeeName.

- Constructor in Employee initializing both fields.

- Getters: int getEmployeeId(), String getEmployeeName().

- Abstract method double calculateSalary().

- FullTimeEmployee: field double monthlySalary, constructor for all values, overrides calculateSalary() to return monthlySalary.

- ContractEmployee: fields int workingDays, double dailyRate, constructor for all values, overrides calculateSalary() to return workingDays × dailyRate.

- In main(), use an Employee reference to hold the right subclass object.

### Input

Line 1: employeeType (1 = full-time, 2 = contract)

Line 2: employeeId employeeName

Line 3: type 1 gives monthlySalary (double); type 2 gives workingDays (int) and dailyRate (double)

### Output

Employee ID: <int>
Employee Name: <string>
Salary: <double, 2 decimals>

### Constraints

1 ≤ employeeType ≤ 2; 1 ≤ employeeId ≤ 100000; 1 ≤ workingDays ≤ 31; 0.0 < monthlySalary ≤ 1000000.0; 0.0 < dailyRate ≤ 100000.0; employeeName has letters only.

### Sample

**Input:**

```text
2
105 Arun
24 1500.0
```

**Output:**

```text
Employee ID: 105
Employee Name: Arun
Salary: 36000.00
```

### Extra test

Input 1 / 101 Ravi / 45000.0 gives Salary 45000.00.

### Gotchas

- Fields must be private; access them only through getters.

- The third input line differs by type, so read it inside the branch.

- Read the name with next(), not nextLine(), to avoid leftover-newline issues.

### Acceptance criteria

- Employee is abstract and cannot be instantiated.

- Both subclasses override calculateSalary().

- main() declares Employee emp and assigns a subclass object to it.

### Checklist

- [ ] Sample worked out by hand

- [ ] Hierarchy sketched

- [ ] Code written

- [ ] Two-decimal formatting verified

- [ ] Sample and extra test pass

- [ ] Edge cases tested

title: Q2: Banking Account Management
body:
**Difficulty: Easy. Phase: 1.**

### Problem

A bank has savings and current accounts, and the amount available is calculated differently for each.

### Required design

- class BankAccount with int accountNumber, double balance, a constructor for both, and double calculateFinalBalance().

- SavingsAccount: field double interestRate; overrides calculateFinalBalance() as balance + (balance × interestRate / 100).

- CurrentAccount: field double overdraftLimit; overrides calculateFinalBalance() as balance + overdraftLimit.

- In main(), use a BankAccount reference.

### Input

Line 1: accountType (1 = savings, 2 = current)

Line 2: accountNumber balance

Line 3: type 1 gives interestRate; type 2 gives overdraftLimit (both double)

### Output

The calculated amount only, with exactly 2 decimals.

### Constraints

1 ≤ accountType ≤ 2; 1 ≤ accountNumber ≤ 1000000; 0.0 < balance ≤ 10000000.0; 0.0 ≤ interestRate ≤ 20.0; 0.0 ≤ overdraftLimit ≤ 500000.0.

### Sample

**Input:**

```text
1
50021 100000.0
6.0
```

**Output:**

```text
106000.00
```

### Extra test

Input 2 / 7001 20000.0 / 5000.0 gives 25000.00.

### Gotchas

- BankAccount is a normal (non-abstract) class, so its own calculateFinalBalance() should return the plain balance.

- Divide by 100 (an int literal is fine here because the other operands are double).

### Acceptance criteria

- Both subclasses call the parent constructor and override the method.

- Output is the number alone, with no label text.

### Checklist

- [ ] Sample worked out by hand

- [ ] Hierarchy sketched

- [ ] Code written

- [ ] Two-decimal formatting verified

- [ ] Sample and extra test pass

- [ ] Edge cases tested

title: Q3: Online Payment Processing
body:
**Difficulty: Easy. Phase: 1.**

### Problem

An online store supports several payment methods, each with a different transaction fee.

### Required design

- interface Payment with double calculateFee(double amount).

- Implementations: CreditCardPayment (2%), UpiPayment (0.5%), WalletPayment (1%).

- Final Amount = Payment Amount + Transaction Fee.

- In main(), use a Payment reference.

### Input

Line 1: paymentType (1 = Credit Card, 2 = UPI, 3 = Wallet)

Line 2: paymentAmount (double)

### Output

Payment Amount: <2 decimals>
Transaction Fee: <2 decimals>
Final Amount: <2 decimals>

### Constraints

1 ≤ paymentType ≤ 3; 0.0 < paymentAmount ≤ 1000000.0.

### Sample

**Input:**

```text
2
10000.0
```

**Output:**

```text
Payment Amount: 10000.00
Transaction Fee: 50.00
Final Amount: 10050.00
```

### Extra tests

1 / 1000.0 gives fee 20.00, final 1020.00.

3 / 2000.0 gives fee 20.00, final 2020.00.

### Gotchas

- Interface methods are implicitly public, so implementations must declare public.

- The final amount is computed in main() (the interface only exposes the fee).

### Acceptance criteria

- Three classes implement Payment.

- Payment p = new ...; is used to call calculateFee.

### Checklist

- [ ] Sample worked out by hand

- [ ] Hierarchy sketched

- [ ] Code written

- [ ] Two-decimal formatting verified

- [ ] Sample and extra tests pass

- [ ] Edge cases tested

title: Q4: Vehicle Rental System
body:
**Difficulty: Easy–Medium. Phase: 2.**

### Problem

A rental company rents cars, bikes and trucks, each with a fixed daily rate.

### Required design

- class Vehicle with double dailyRate, a constructor initializing it, double calculateRentalCharge(int rentalDays) and String getVehicleType().

- Subclasses Car (1500.0), Bike (600.0), Truck (3000.0).

- Each subclass calls the parent constructor with super(...) and overrides getVehicleType().

- Rental charge must use the inherited calculateRentalCharge() (dailyRate × rentalDays); do not override it.

- In main(), use a Vehicle reference.

### Input

Line 1: vehicleType (1 = Car, 2 = Bike, 3 = Truck)

Line 2: rentalDays (int)

### Output

Vehicle Type: <string>
Rental Charge: <2 decimals>

### Constraints

1 ≤ vehicleType ≤ 3; 1 ≤ rentalDays ≤ 30.

### Sample

**Input:**

```text
1
5
```

**Output:**

```text
Vehicle Type: Car
Rental Charge: 7500.00
```

### Extra tests

2 / 3 gives Bike, 1800.00.

3 / 10 gives Truck, 30000.00.

### Gotchas

- The daily rate is fixed per subclass and passed through super(rate); it is not read from input.

- Overriding calculateRentalCharge would violate the requirement.

### Acceptance criteria

- Each subclass constructor contains a super(...) call.

- calculateRentalCharge exists only in Vehicle.

### Checklist

- [ ] Sample worked out by hand

- [ ] Hierarchy sketched

- [ ] Code written

- [ ] Two-decimal formatting verified

- [ ] Sample and extra tests pass

- [ ] Edge cases tested

title: Q5: Employee Performance Bonus
body:
**Difficulty: Hard. Phase: 3 (do last).**

### Problem

Bonuses are calculated differently for technical and sales employees. The design must show both method overriding and method overloading.

### Required design

- class Employee with String employeeName, a constructor initializing it, double calculateBonus() and double calculateBonus(double amount).

- calculateBonus() must be overridden by the subclasses.

- TechnicalEmployee: fields double basicSalary, int rating; constructor for all fields.

- Override calculateBonus(): basicSalary × rating × 2 / 100.

- Overload calculateBonus(double salary, int employeeRating).

- SalesEmployee: field double salesAmount; constructor for all fields.

- Override calculateBonus(): salesAmount × 3 / 100.

- Provide calculateBonus(double amount) returning 3% of the supplied amount.

- In main(), use an Employee reference.

### Input

Line 1: employeeType (1 = Technical, 2 = Sales)

Line 2: type 1 gives employeeName basicSalary rating; type 2 gives employeeName salesAmount

### Output

Employee Name: <string>
Bonus: <2 decimals>
Total Earnings: <2 decimals>

Technical: Total = Basic Salary + Bonus. Sales: Total = Sales Amount + Bonus.

### Constraints

1 ≤ employeeType ≤ 2; 0.0 < basicSalary ≤ 1000000.0; 0.0 < salesAmount ≤ 5000000.0; 1 ≤ rating ≤ 5; employeeName has letters only.

### Sample

**Input:**

```text
1
Kumar 50000.0 4
```

**Output:**

```text
Employee Name: Kumar
Bonus: 4000.00
Total Earnings: 54000.00
```

### Extra test

Input 2 / Meena 200000.0 gives Bonus 6000.00, Total 206000.00.

### Gotchas

- SalesEmployee.calculateBonus(double) has the same signature as the base method, so it is technically an override, not a new overload. The genuine overload in this question is TechnicalEmployee.calculateBonus(double, int).

- A base-type reference cannot call the subclass-only overload calculateBonus(double, int) without a cast. Decide where to demonstrate it (for example, call it on a TechnicalEmployee variable, or cast).

- Give the base class sensible default bodies (for example return 0.0) so it compiles and stays concrete.

- Technical and sales inputs have different shapes on line 2.

### Acceptance criteria

- Overriding is demonstrated through an Employee reference.

- At least one true overload exists (calculateBonus(double, int)).

- The total earnings formula differs correctly by employee type.

### Checklist

- [ ] Sample worked out by hand

- [ ] Hierarchy sketched

- [ ] Overload vs override decisions written down

- [ ] Code written

- [ ] Two-decimal formatting verified

- [ ] Sample and extra test pass

- [ ] Edge cases tested (rating 1 and 5)

title: Q6: Food Delivery Order
body:
**Difficulty: Easy. Phase: 1.**

### Problem

A food delivery platform offers regular and express delivery with different charges.

### Required design

- class Delivery with double orderAmount, a constructor, and double calculateDeliveryCharge().

- RegularDelivery: overrides to return orderAmount + 40.0.

- ExpressDelivery: overrides to return orderAmount + 80.0 + (orderAmount × 5 / 100).

- In main(), use a Delivery reference.

### Input

Line 1: deliveryType (1 = Regular, 2 = Express)

Line 2: orderAmount (double)

### Output

The final charge only, with exactly 2 decimals.

### Constraints

1 ≤ deliveryType ≤ 2; 0.0 < orderAmount ≤ 500000.0.

### Sample

**Input:**

```text
2
1000.0
```

**Output:**

```text
1130.00
```

### Extra test

Input 1 / 500.0 gives 540.00.

### Gotchas

- The "final charge" includes the order amount, not just the delivery fee.

- Output is the number alone, with no label.

### Acceptance criteria

- Both subclasses override calculateDeliveryCharge().

- A Delivery reference holds the subclass object.

### Checklist

- [ ] Sample worked out by hand

- [ ] Hierarchy sketched

- [ ] Code written

- [ ] Two-decimal formatting verified

- [ ] Sample and extra test pass

- [ ] Edge cases tested

title: Q7: Employee Access and Permission System
body:
**Difficulty: Easy–Medium. Phase: 2.**

### Problem

An enterprise application grants different access permissions by role, with several implementations of one access-control contract.

### Required design

- interface AccessControl with String getRole(), int getAccessLevel(), boolean canAccess(int requiredLevel).

- Implementations: Developer (level 1), Manager (level 2), Administrator (level 3).

- canAccess(requiredLevel) returns true when the employee's level ≥ requiredLevel, otherwise false.

- In main(), use an AccessControl reference.

### Input

Line 1: roleType (1 = Developer, 2 = Manager, 3 = Administrator)

Line 2: requiredLevel (int)

### Output

Role: <string>
Access Level: <int>
Can Access: <true|false>

### Constraints

1 ≤ roleType ≤ 3; 1 ≤ requiredLevel ≤ 3.

### Sample

**Input:**

```text
2
3
```

**Output:**

```text
Role: Manager
Access Level: 2
Can Access: false
```

### Extra tests

3 / 3 gives Administrator, 3, true.

1 / 2 gives Developer, 1, false.

### Gotchas

- Print the boolean as lowercase true or false; Java does this by default when printing a boolean.

- Use >=, not >.

### Acceptance criteria

- Three classes implement all three interface methods.

- Output labels match exactly.

### Checklist

- [ ] Sample worked out by hand

- [ ] Hierarchy sketched

- [ ] Code written

- [ ] Sample and extra tests pass

- [ ] Edge cases tested (equal levels)

title: Q8: Online Course Fee Calculation
body:
**Difficulty: Medium. Phase: 2.**

### Problem

An online learning platform gives a different discount per course category.

### Required design

- abstract class Course with double courseFee, a constructor, abstract double calculateDiscount(), abstract String getCourseType(), and a concrete double calculateFinalFee() returning courseFee - calculateDiscount().

- Subclasses: ProgrammingCourse (10%), DataScienceCourse (15%), CloudCourse (5%).

- Each subclass overrides calculateDiscount() and getCourseType().

- In main(), use a Course reference.

### Input

Line 1: courseType (1 = Programming, 2 = Data Science, 3 = Cloud)

Line 2: courseFee (double)

### Output

Course Type: <string>
Discount: <2 decimals>
Final Fee: <2 decimals>

### Constraints

1 ≤ courseType ≤ 3; 0.0 < courseFee ≤ 1000000.0.

### Sample

**Input:**

```text
2
50000.0
```

**Output:**

```text
Course Type: Data Science
Discount: 7500.00
Final Fee: 42500.00
```

### Extra tests

1 / 10000.0 gives Programming, 1000.00, 9000.00.

3 / 20000.0 gives Cloud, 1000.00, 19000.00.

### Gotchas

- calculateFinalFee() lives in the abstract class and calls the abstract calculateDiscount(); subclasses do not override it.

- The course type string for type 2 is exactly Data Science (with a space).

### Acceptance criteria

- Course is abstract with two abstract methods and one concrete method.

- All three subclasses override both abstract methods.

### Checklist

- [ ] Sample worked out by hand

- [ ] Hierarchy sketched

- [ ] Code written

- [ ] Two-decimal formatting verified

- [ ] Sample and extra tests pass

- [ ] Edge cases tested

title: Q9: Hospital Billing System
body:
**Difficulty: Medium. Phase: 3.**

### Problem

A hospital charges differently by service type. Emergency consultations also include test charges.

### Required design

- abstract class Doctor with double consultationCharge, a constructor, abstract String getDoctorType(), and concrete double calculateTotalBill(double testCharges) whose base version returns only the consultation charge.

- Subclasses: GeneralPhysician (500.0), Specialist (1000.0), EmergencyDoctor (1500.0).

- EmergencyDoctor overrides calculateTotalBill(double testCharges) to return consultationCharge + testCharges.

- Every subclass overrides getDoctorType().

- In main(), use a Doctor reference.

### Input

Line 1: doctorType (1 = General Physician, 2 = Specialist, 3 = Emergency Doctor)

Line 2: testCharges (double)

### Output

Doctor Type: <string>
Consultation Charge: <2 decimals>
Test Charges: <2 decimals>
Total Bill: <2 decimals>

### Constraints

1 ≤ doctorType ≤ 3; 0.0 ≤ testCharges ≤ 100000.0.

### Sample

**Input:**

```text
3
2500.0
```

**Output:**

```text
Doctor Type: Emergency Doctor
Consultation Charge: 1500.00
Test Charges: 2500.00
Total Bill: 4000.00
```

### Extra tests

1 / 0.0 gives General Physician, 500.00, 0.00, total 500.00.

2 / 300.0 gives Specialist, 1000.00, 300.00, total 1000.00 (test charges are printed but not added).

### Gotchas

- For non-emergency doctors, print the input test charges but exclude them from the total.

- Consultation charges are fixed per subclass and passed via super(...).

- Only EmergencyDoctor overrides calculateTotalBill.

### Acceptance criteria

- Doctor has one abstract and one concrete method.

- Overriding a concrete method is demonstrated in EmergencyDoctor.

### Checklist

- [ ] Sample worked out by hand

- [ ] Hierarchy sketched

- [ ] Code written

- [ ] Two-decimal formatting verified

- [ ] Sample and extra tests pass

- [ ] Edge cases tested (testCharges 0.0)

title: Q10: E-Commerce Product Pricing
body:
**Difficulty: Easy. Phase: 1.**

### Problem

An e-commerce platform applies a different discount percentage per product category.

### Required design

- class Product with int productId, String productName, double price, a constructor initializing all three, and double calculateDiscount().

- Subclasses: ElectronicsProduct (12%), ClothingProduct (20%), GroceryProduct (5%), each overriding calculateDiscount().

- Final Price = Price − Discount.

- In main(), use a Product reference.

### Input

Line 1: productType (1 = Electronics, 2 = Clothing, 3 = Grocery)

Line 2: productId productName price

### Output

Product ID: <int>
Product Name: <string>
Discount: <2 decimals>
Final Price: <2 decimals>

### Constraints

1 ≤ productType ≤ 3; 1 ≤ productId ≤ 1000000; 0.0 < price ≤ 10000000.0; productName has letters only.

### Sample

**Input:**

```text
1
501 Laptop 75000.0
```

**Output:**

```text
Product ID: 501
Product Name: Laptop
Discount: 9000.00
Final Price: 66000.00
```

### Extra tests

2 / 12 Shirt 2000.0 gives discount 400.00, final 1600.00.

3 / 9 Rice 100.0 gives discount 5.00, final 95.00.

### Gotchas

- Read in the order nextInt(), next(), nextDouble().

- Discount is a percentage of price, not a flat value.

### Acceptance criteria

- Three subclasses override calculateDiscount().

- Product details print before the discount and final price.

### Checklist

- [ ] Sample worked out by hand

- [ ] Hierarchy sketched

- [ ] Code written

- [ ] Two-decimal formatting verified

- [ ] Sample and extra tests pass

- [ ] Edge cases tested
